jobs.title: Environmental Science Analyst
jobs.description:
Overview:

Kimley-Horn is looking for Environmental Science graduates with 1+ years of experience to join our Oakland, CA office! This is not a remote position.

Responsibilities:

* Assist with the preparation of CEQA and NEPA environmental documents.
* Support project teams with environmental research, data collection, and technical analyses.
* Coordinate with environmental specialists, planners, engineers, and project managers.
* Help prepare permit applications and regulatory agency submittals.
* Conduct desktop research related to environmental regulations, permitting requirements, and project constraints.
* Assist with field investigations, site visits, and environmental documentation efforts.
* Support proposal development, project pursuits, and business development activities.
* Maintain project files, schedules, and deliverables in accordance with Kimley-Horn standards.
* Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams supporting infrastructure, transportation, utility, water, and energy projects.

Qualifications:

* Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Studies, Planning, Biology, Geography, Natural Resources, or a related field.
* 1+ year of relevant environmental consulting, planning, or internship experience.
* Interest in environmental compliance, permitting, and impact assessment.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills.
* Excellent organizational and time-management abilities.
* Experience with Microsoft Office applications.
* Ability to work effectively in a collaborative, team-oriented environment.

Why Kimley-Horn?:

At Kimley-Horn, we do things differently. People, clients, and employees are at the forefront of who we are. Clients know we prioritize achieving their goals and growing their success. Employees know our culture and approach to business are built on a desire to provide an environment for everyone to flourish. Our commitment to quality is only as good as the people behind it— that’s why we welcome and develop passionate, hardworking, and proactive employees. We take pride in how our employee retention, robust benefits package, and company values have led to Kimley-Horn’s placement on the Fortune “100 Best Companies to Work” list for 19 years!

*Key Benefits at Kimley-Horn*

* Exceptional Retirement Plan: 2-to1- company match on up to 4% of eligible compensation (salary + bonus) and additional profit-sharing contribution.
* Comprehensive Health Coverage: Low-cost medical, dental, and vision insurance options.
* Time Off: Personal leave, flexible scheduling, floating holidays, and half-day Fridays.
* Financial Wellness: Student loan matching in our 401(k), and performance-based bonuses.
* Professional Development: Tuition reimbursement and extensive internal training programs.
* Family-Friendly Benefits: New Parent Leave, family building benefits, and childcare resources.

jobs.title: Associate Consultant, Air Quality
jobs.description:
**Company Description**

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. No sponsorship is available for this position.

**Inviting bright minds**

Do you want to develop your excellence in an open, collaborative and creative culture? We work to create a sustainable future and our inspiring projects and innovative solutions aim to set the standard among our peers. You will join a global company that has been growing successfully since its founding in 1945. Together, we lead and leave a positive impact on societies, companies and people around the world.  
  
Ramboll is seeking an Air Quality Intern to join the firm’s offices in Los Angeles or Irvine, California, or Phoenix, Arizona in Spring/Summer 2027. If you are detail-oriented, self-motivated and enjoy thinking “outside-of-the-box,” please apply! If you can work in a team, apply analytical skills, and are looking to get your hands dirty (literally and figuratively), then you may find Ramboll to be an ideal place to start your career.

 **Job Description**

**You will join our Environment & Health** **department**

As our new Entry Level Air Quality Consultant you will be part of the Air & Climate Service Line within Ramboll’s Environment & Health Division. This group consists of like-minded individuals who are passionate about air and climate issues and assisting Ramboll’s clients with their most challenging problems. The Air & Climate team consults with clients across various industries on a range of topics, including but not limited to emissions estimation, air dispersion modeling, human health risk assessment, climate change, permitting, and compliance.

Your key tasks and responsibilities will be:

* + Preparing emissions calculations
  + Conducting air quality reviews of emissions reduction or control
  + Assisting in preparing major and minor source permit applications and environmental impact reports
  + Critically reviewing and interpreting local, state, and federal environmental regulations

  
**Qualifications**

**Your starting point for constant growth**

From the moment you join Ramboll, we will support your personal and professional development so that you grow with the company. For this role, we believe your starting point is:

* B.S. or M.S. in Chemical, Mechanical, Civil, or Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, Atmospheric Science, or a science degree with air quality course work with a GPA of 3.5 or higher
* Strong computing skills including high level use of spreadsheets and word processing
* Strong written/verbal communication, problem-solving and organization skills
* Ability to understand and interpret environmental regulations
* Database and GIS skills are preferred but not required

  
**Additional Information**

**Welcome to our Environment & Health division**  
Ramboll develops innovative, scientifically sound solutions that help increase live ability by reducing pollution and restoring natural environments. One of the world’s leading environmental and health consultancies, our bright minds are trusted by clients to manage their most challenging environmental, health and social issues.

**Ramboll in the Americas**

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll in the Americas has thousands of experts working across more than 70 offices. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Environment & Health, Water, Energy, and Planning & Urban Design.

**Salary Transparency Statement**

At Ramboll, we are committed to fair and transparent compensation practices that support our people and our purpose of creating sustainable societies. The anticipated base salary range for this position is $64,404 to $80,505 yearly. This range reflects the compensation we reasonably expect to offer at the time of posting. Actual compensation will vary based on factors such as location, skills, experience, education, and internal equity. Because we operate across multiple U.S. markets, pay may differ depending on the cost of labor in specific locations. In addition to base salary, this position may be eligible for bonus, overtime or other forms of compensation and we offer a comprehensive benefits package that supports well-being, professional development, and work-life balance. Our recruiters are happy to share more about the specific salary range and total rewards package applicable to your location during the hiring process.

**Where People Flourish**

Our mission is to create sustainable societies where people and nature flourish. This means that a culture of inclusion is embedded in everything we do. Our people bring diverse backgrounds and experiences to the company, enabling us to deliver innovative and forward-thinking solutions to our clients. We also know how important it is to achieve the right balance of where, when, and how much you work. At Ramboll, we offer flexibility as part of our positive and inclusive approach to work. We are committed to equal employment opportunity, regardless of age, disability or medical condition, gender identity, marriage and domestic partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, ancestry, or national origin, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation, military service and veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. Ramboll wants to ensure opportunities are accessible to candidates with disabilities. So, please let us know if there are any changes we could make to the application process to make it more comfortable for you. You can contact us at job.advert.accessibility@ramboll.com with such requests.

**How to apply**

Apply online. Atta

### **Job Description and Duties**

**ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST – SAN LUIS OBISPO COAST DISTRICT / MORRO BAY FIELD OFFICE**

The reporting location for this position is the Morro Bay field office. This position will work under the general supervision of the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisor).

The Environmental Scientist assists in a variety of responsible professional scientific office and field work. The Environmental Scientist independently performs assigned environmental and natural resource management analysis, research, surveys, and studies; writes final reports; prepares regulatory and compliance documents; enforces environmental law and regulations; prepares non-routine correspondence and answer non-routine questionsfrom the public. The Environmental Scientist performs a variety of tasks including the more responsible, varied, and complex assignments. The Environmental Scientist will be able to work independently and will be assigned lead responsibilities for State and/or federally listed species. Tasks will further Natural Resources Division projects and programs as identified by the Senior Environmental Specialist.

Training and Development Assignments may be considered.

This position is designed to as not telework eligible.

**State housing is not available.** For further information regarding this position, please contact Katie Drexhage at (805) 712-4768 or Katie.Drexhage@parks.ca.gov.

### **Job Description and Duties**

Under the supervision of the Beaver Restoration Program Supervisor, the incumbent will serve as part of the Beaver Restoration Program, implementing beaver restoration projects to support ecosystem conservation, habitat restoration, species conservation, and improve climate change, drought, and wildfire resilience throughout California. Tasks include conducting pre-trapping beaver surveillance, live-trapping and transporting beavers to CDFW's husbandry facilities, daily animal care and pen cleaning during quarantine, beaver translocations and pre- and post-release monitoring of the ecosystem and translocated beavers, maintenance of equipment and animal husbandry facilities, data collection, entry, and management, conducting beaver surveys throughout the state to help determine the current distribution of beavers in California, as well as assisting with image cataloguing in Wildlife Insights to improve the species identification algorithm for species commonly encountered in California’s wetland ecosystems.

**Personal Leave Program:** Effective July 1, 2025, state employees are subject to temporary salary reductions ranging from 2% to 4.62% in exchange for Personal Leave Program (PLP) hours. Please note that the salary ranges listed in this Job Control may not reflect these reductions associated with the 2025 Personal Leave Program.

  

Please follow the link for more information regarding the 2025 Personal Leave program:

  

Personal Leave Program - Human Resources - CalHR.

Environmental Scientist: Exam Bulletin Link

**This position is a 12-month Limited Term (LT) and may be extended up to 24 months or become permanent.**

During this 12-month Limited Term assignment, you will receive full health, dental, and vision benefits! You will also earn State Service and accrue monthly leave credits.

  

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Working Conditions**

Must be willing to work long, irregular hours, including early mornings, evenings, and weekends due to the species involved (e.g., nighttime tracking, evening trap sets, daily trap checks). Regular travel in state vehicles (> 40%) and some overnight travel (up to 15%) will be required.

  

Must possess valid Driver's License and be able to safely and effectively operate watercraft and Utility Task Vehicles (UTV)s, as well as tow trailers. This job requires daily operation of State vehicles to reach field sites, regular use of kayaks, and occasional operation of UTVs and motorized watercraft. Must wear Department uniform. Field activities may involve strenuous physical activity, hiking long distances in variable weather conditions, and/or camping in remote field sites. If assigned, must complete wildlife capture and restraint training within 12 months of hire. Must be willing and able to competently use and possess wildlife restraint drugs and equipment; handle live animals and carcasses. When not working in the field, must be able to work in the office setting at least 4 days per week, using a computer keyboard in a sitting and/or standing position several hours a day, unless State or CDFW policies require or allow otherwise.

  

### **Position Details**

JC-534521

jobs.title: Chemical Safety Specialist
jobs.description:
Under general supervision of the Chemical Hygiene Officer at the UCLA Office of Environment, Health & Safety and in accordance
  
with State & Federal regulations, the Chemical Safety Specialist applies technical knowledge to implement, administer, and
  
continuously improve comprehensive laboratory and chemical safety programs supporting research, (indirect) instructional, and
  
operational activities across UCLA. The incumbent provides technical consultation to the faculty, principal investigators,
  
researchers, staff, students, and campus departments regarding chemical, laboratory, and research safety requirements.

  

Responsibilities include developing and implementing Research Safety Management Plans; conducting lab hazard assessments
  
and compliance evaluations; developing and delivering safety training; participating in hazardous materials emergency response;
  
conducting incident investigations; supporting continuous process improvement initiatives; and performing other duties as
  
assigned.

  

Functional assignments may include support for research laboratories, engineering laboratories, medical and health sciences,
  
physical sciences, nanotechnology, hazardous materials, chemical hygiene, laboratory commissioning, laboratory design review,
  
or other specialized research safety programs.

  

This master job description establishes the core duties and responsibilities of the Laboratory Safety Professional position. Specific
  
program assignments, portfolios, departments, and specialized technical responsibilities may be assigned or modified by
  
management based on operational needs, organizational priorities, employee experience, and requirements. Such assignments
  
do not alter the overall classification or primary purpose of the position.

  

This is an in-person position.

  

The incumbent will work under general supervision and independently perform the full range of professional responsibilities
  
within assigned program areas. Their work is reviewed upon completion to ensure established standards are met and that
  
application of professional/technical judgment is sound, and for accuracy, consistency, and achievement of program objectives.

  
**Salary & Compensation**
  
  
\*UCLA provides a full pay range. Actual salary offers consider factors, including budget, prior experience, skills, knowledge, abilities, education, licensure and certifications, and other business considerations. Salary offers at the top of the range are not common. Visit UC Benefit package to discover benefits that start on day one, and UC Total Compensation Estimator to calculate the total compensation value with benefits.
  
**Qualifications**  
  

* 2 years professional experience in a comprehensive environmental health and safety program, or an equivalent combination of education and experience (Required)

* Ability to initiate and maintain cooperative working relationships with co-workers, supervisors, and managers. Skill in establishing rapport and gaining trust of others. Ability to work harmoniously and as a team player, thrive in a team-based environment, and skill in fostering teamwork among others. (Required)

* Skill in exchanging ideas, information, and opinions with others to formulate policies and programs and/or arrive jointly at decisions, conclusions, or solutions. Skill in working as part of a team; collaborating with colleagues. (Required)

* Ability to speak clearly on a one-to-one basis using appropriate vocabulary and grammar to obtain information, explain procedures and situations, and persuade others to comply with regulations and guidelines. Skill in speaking with persons of various social, cultural, economic and educational backgrounds. Ability to make oral presentations that communicate information and explain procedures accurately to faculty, staff and students. (Required)

* Skill in handling a variety of job-related topics on short or no notice. Ability to set priorities which accurately reflect the importance of the job responsibilities. (Required)

* Experience working independently, using sound judgment under pressure; working effectively with faculty, university administrators, staff and students in a large, complex organization. (Required)

* Demonstrated critical thinking and analytical skills, understanding of consensus building and group dynamics, diplomacy and negotiation. (Required)

* Using proactive attitude and initiative, demonstrate ability to perform independently and effectively under conditions of fluctuating workloads and a variety of assigned duties. Ability to complete assignments independently or with minimal supervision. Ability to take directions and follow through on details. (Required)

* Sufficient advanced writing skills to prepare clear, concise, logical, and grammatically correct technical reports, analysis, correspondence, etc. for management, faculty, staff, and regulatory agencies. (Required)

* Ability to work in person/on site. On occasion, may need to work during non-business hours, weekends, and holidays. (Required)

* Ability to develop adult education materials as it relates to chemical and laboratory safety principles. (Required)

* Advanced knowledge of federal, state and local health and safety regulations and guidelines governing laboratory safety, biological safety and animal use operation. (Preferred)

* Advanced knowledge of risk mitigation, industrial hygiene principles, chemical safety controls, exposure evaluation, exposure monitoring, and occupational health processes. (Preferred)

  
**Education, Licenses, Certifications & Personal Affiliations**  
  

* Bachelor's Degree in an appropriate scientific field such chemistry, biochemistry, physics, biology, industrial hygiene, safety, engineering, or a closely related field (Required) Or

* an equivalent combination of education and experience. (Required)

* Must possess, upon hire, and maintain a valid CA noncommercial Class C License in accordanc

This group consists of like-minded individuals who are passionate about air and climate issues and assisting Ramboll’s clients with their most challenging problems. The Air & Climate team consults with clients across various industries on a range of topics, including but not limited to emissions estimation, air dispersion modeling, human health risk assessment, climate change, permitting, and compliance.

Your key tasks and responsibilities will be:

* + Preparing emissions calculations
  + Conducting air quality reviews of emissions reduction or control
  + Assisting in preparing major and minor source permit applications and environmental impact reports
  + Critically reviewing and interpreting local, state, and federal environmental regulations

  
**Qualifications**

**Your starting point for constant growth**

From the moment you join Ramboll, we will support your personal and professional development so that you grow with the company. For this role, we believe your starting point is:

* B.S. or M.S. in Chemical, Mechanical, Civil, or Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, Atmospheric Science, or a science degree with air quality course work with a GPA of 3.5 or higher
* Strong computing skills including high level use of spreadsheets and word processing
* Strong written/verbal communication, problem-solving and organization skills
* Ability to understand and interpret environmental regulations
* Database and GIS skills are preferred but not required

  
**Additional Information**

**Welcome to our Environment & Health division**  
Ramboll develops innovative, scientifically sound solutions that help increase live ability by reducing pollution and restoring natural environments. One of the world’s leading environmental and health consultancies, our bright minds are trusted by clients to manage their most challenging environmental, health and social issues.

**Ramboll in the Americas**

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll in the Americas has thousands of experts working across more than 70 offices. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Environment & Health, Water, Energy, and Planning & Urban Design.

**Salary Transparency Statement**

At Ramboll, we are committed to fair and transparent compensation practices that support our people and our purpose of creating sustainable societies. The anticipated base salary range for this position is $64,404 to $80,505 yearly. This range reflects the compensation we reasonably expect to offer at the time of posting. Actual compensation will vary based on factors such as location, skills, experience, education, and internal equity. Because we operate across multiple U.S. markets, pay may differ depending on the cost of labor in specific locations. In addition to base salary, this position may be eligible for bonus, overtime or other forms of compensation and we offer a comprehensive benefits package that supports well-being, professional development, and work-life balance. Our recruiters are happy to share more about the specific salary range and total rewards package applicable to your location during the hiring process.

**Where People Flourish**

Our mission is to create sustainable societies where people and nature flourish. This means that a culture of inclusion is embedded in everything we do. Our people bring diverse backgrounds and experiences to the company, enabling us to deliver innovative and forward-thinking solutions to our clients. We also know how important it is to achieve the right balance of where, when, and how much you work. At Ramboll, we offer flexibility as part of our positive and inclusive approach to work. We are committed to equal employment opportunity, regardless of age, disability or medical condition, gender identity, marriage and domestic partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, ancestry, or national origin, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation, military service and veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. Ramboll wants to ensure opportunities are accessible to candidates with disabilities. So, please let us know if there are any changes we could make to the application process to make it more comfortable for you. You can contact us at job.advert.accessibility@ramboll.com with such requests.

**How to apply**

Apply online. Atta

new_jobs.title: Chemical Safety Specialist
new_jobs.description:
Under general supervision of the Chemical Hygiene Officer at the UCLA Office of Environment, Health & Safety and in accordance
  
with State & Federal regulations, the Chemical Safety Specialist applies technical knowledge to implement, administer, and
  
continuously improve comprehensive laboratory and chemical safety programs supporting research, (indirect) instructional, and
  
operational activities across UCLA. The incumbent provides technical consultation to the faculty, principal investigators,
  
researchers, staff, students, and campus departments regarding chemical, laboratory, and research safety requirements.

  

Responsibilities include developing and implementing Research Safety Management Plans; conducting lab hazard assessments
  
and compliance evaluations; developing and delivering safety training; participating in hazardous materials emergency response;
  
conducting incident investigations; supporting continuous process improvement initiatives; and performing other duties as
  
assigned.

  

Functional assignments may include support for research laboratories, engineering laboratories, medical and health sciences,
  
physical sciences, nanotechnology, hazardous materials, chemical hygiene, laboratory commissioning, laboratory design review,
  
or other specialized research safety programs.

  

This master job description establishes the core duties and responsibilities of the Laboratory Safety Professional position. Specific
  
program assignments, portfolios, departments, and specialized technical responsibilities may be assigned or modified by
  
management based on operational needs, organizational priorities, employee experience, and requirements. Such assignments
  
do not alter the overall classification or primary purpose of the position.

  

This is an in-person position.

  

The incumbent will work under general supervision and independently perform the full range of professional responsibilities
  
within assigned program areas. Their work is reviewed upon completion to ensure established standards are met and that
  
application of professional/technical judgment is sound, and for accuracy, consistency, and achievement of program objectives.

  
**Salary & Compensation**
  
  
\*UCLA provides a full pay range. Actual salary offers consider factors, including budget, prior experience, skills, knowledge, abilities, education, licensure and certifications, and other business considerations. Salary offers at the top of the range are not common. Visit UC Benefit package to discover benefits that start on day one, and UC Total Compensation Estimator to calculate the total compensation value with benefits.
  
**Qualifications**  
  

* 2 years professional experience in a comprehensive environmental health and safety program, or an equivalent combination of education and experience (Required)

* Ability to initiate and maintain cooperative working relationships with co-workers, supervisors, and managers. Skill in establishing rapport and gaining trust of others. Ability to work harmoniously and as a team player, thrive in a team-based environment, and skill in fostering teamwork among others. (Required)

* Skill in exchanging ideas, information, and opinions with others to formulate policies and programs and/or arrive jointly at decisions, conclusions, or solutions. Skill in working as part of a team; collaborating with colleagues. (Required)

* Ability to speak clearly on a one-to-one basis using appropriate vocabulary and grammar to obtain information, explain procedures and situations, and persuade others to comply with regulations and guidelines. Skill in speaking with persons of various social, cultural, economic and educational backgrounds. Ability to make oral presentations that communicate information and explain procedures accurately to faculty, staff and students. (Required)

* Skill in handling a variety of job-related topics on short or no notice. Ability to set priorities which accurately reflect the importance of the job responsibilities. (Required)

* Experience working independently, using sound judgment under pressure; working effectively with faculty, university administrators, staff and students in a large, complex organization. (Required)

* Demonstrated critical thinking and analytical skills, understanding of consensus building and group dynamics, diplomacy and negotiation. (Required)

* Using proactive attitude and initiative, demonstrate ability to perform independently and effectively under conditions of fluctuating workloads and a variety of assigned duties. Ability to complete assignments independently or with minimal supervision. Ability to take directions and follow through on details. (Required)

* Sufficient advanced writing skills to prepare clear, concise, logical, and grammatically correct technical reports, analysis, correspondence, etc. for management, faculty, staff, and regulatory agencies. (Required)

* Ability to work in person/on site. On occasion, may need to work during non-business hours, weekends, and holidays. (Required)

* Ability to develop adult education materials as it relates to chemical and laboratory safety principles. (Required)

* Advanced knowledge of federal, state and local health and safety regulations and guidelines governing laboratory safety, biological safety and animal use operation. (Preferred)

* Advanced knowledge of risk mitigation, industrial hygiene principles, chemical safety controls, exposure evaluation, exposure monitoring, and occupational health processes. (Preferred)

  
**Education, Licenses, Certifications & Personal Affiliations**  
  

* Bachelor's Degree in an appropriate scientific field such chemistry, biochemistry, physics, biology, industrial hygiene, safety, engineering, or a closely related field (Required) Or

* an equivalent combination of education and experience. (Required)
